nodes.title: Circular Motion Basics
points: Uniform circular motion (UCM): constant speed, but velocity changes direction continuously.
UCM is an accelerated motion: acceleration is centripetal, directed towards the centre.
Angular displacement θ is measured in radian (rad). 1 rev = 2π rad = 360°.
Angular velocity ω is an axial vector. Its direction is given by the right-hand thumb rule.
Frequency n = 1/T. Unit of n is Hz (s⁻¹). Unit of ω is rad/s.
In UCM, the angular acceleration α is zero and the tangential acceleration is zero.

nodes.title: Angular Kinematics & Accelerations
points: Angular acceleration α = dω/dt. Unit: rad/s². It is an axial vector.
Rotational equations are analogues of linear equations: replace s→θ, v→ω, a→α.
Tangential acceleration aₜ = rα acts along the tangent. Centripetal a꜀ = ω²r acts towards the centre.
Net acceleration in non-uniform circular motion: a = √(aₜ² + a꜀²).
Number of rotations in time t = θ/2π.

nodes.title: Centripetal & Centrifugal Force
points: Centripetal force acts towards the centre. It is a real force, supplied by tension, gravity, friction or normal force.
Centripetal force does zero work because it is always ⊥ to displacement.
Centrifugal force is a pseudo (fictitious) force. It acts outward and is felt only in the rotating frame.
Centrifugal force is equal in magnitude and opposite to centripetal force. They are NOT an action–reaction pair.
Examples: a cyclist leaning on a turn, a washing machine dryer, a cream separator.

nodes.title: Banking of Roads
points: Banking: the outer edge is raised so the horizontal component of N provides centripetal force.
On a frictionless banked road: N cosθ = mg and N sinθ = mv²/r.
The optimum speed is independent of the mass of the vehicle.
Friction increases the maximum safe speed on a banked road.
Railway tracks are banked by raising the outer rail. Cyclists lean inward to get the same effect.

nodes.title: Conical Pendulum & Vertical Circle
points: Conical pendulum: the bob moves in a horizontal circle. T cosθ = mg and T sinθ = mv²/r.
Period of a conical pendulum depends on L cosθ and g. It does not depend on the mass.
Vertical circle: speed is not constant. It is maximum at the bottom and minimum at the top.
Tension is maximum at the bottom and minimum at the top.
Minimum speed at the top to complete the circle is √(rg), where tension = 0.
Minimum speed at the bottom is √(5rg). Difference in tension (bottom − top) = 6mg.

nodes.title: Moment of Inertia & Theorems
points: Moment of inertia (M.I.) is the rotational analogue of mass. It measures resistance to a change in rotation.
SI unit of I is kg m². Dimensions are [M¹L²T⁰]. It is a scalar for a given axis.
I depends on mass, its distribution, and the position of the axis. It does NOT depend on ω.
Radius of gyration K is the distance at which the whole mass, if concentrated, gives the same I.
Parallel axis theorem applies to any body. Perpendicular axis theorem applies only to planar (lamina) bodies.
In the parallel axis theorem, the axes must be parallel and one must pass through the centre of mass.

nodes.title: M.I. of Standard Bodies (Must Memorise)
points: Ring or hollow cylinder about its own axis: MR². This is the maximum for a given M and R.
Disc or solid cylinder about its axis: ½MR².
Ring or disc about a diameter: Ring = ½MR², Disc = ¼MR².
Solid sphere about a diameter: 2MR²/5. Hollow sphere: 2MR²/3.
Thin rod about its centre: ML²/12. About one end: ML²/3.
Tip: K²/R² values are 1 (ring), ½ (disc), 2/5 (solid sphere), 2/3 (hollow sphere).
Tip: for the same M and R, I order is ring > disc > solid sphere.

nodes.title: Torque & Angular Momentum
points: Torque is the turning effect of a force. It is a vector with direction given by r × F.
SI unit of torque is N m. Dimensions are [M¹L²T⁻²], the same as work but a different quantity.
A couple is a pair of equal, opposite, non-collinear forces. Its torque is force × perpendicular distance.
Angular momentum L = r × p. SI unit is kg m²/s. Dimensions are [M¹L²T⁻¹].
Torque equals the rate of change of angular momentum: τ = dL/dt.
If net external torque = 0, then L is conserved. Hence a skater spins faster when arms are pulled in.
When I decreases, ω increases because I₁ω₁ = I₂ω₂.

nodes.title: Rotational KE & Rolling Motion
points: Rotational kinetic energy = ½Iω². Total KE of a rolling body = translational KE + rotational KE.
Pure rolling: the contact point is at instantaneous rest, so v = Rω.
On an incline, the body with the smallest K²/R² reaches the bottom first.
Order of speed down an incline: solid sphere > disc > hollow sphere > ring.
Acceleration down an incline is independent of mass and radius. It depends only on K²/R² and θ.
For a sliding block (no rolling), a = g sinθ. Rolling bodies are always slower.

nodes.title: MHT-CET Traps, Shortcuts & Memory Tips
points: Trap: centripetal and centrifugal forces never act on the same body in the same frame.
Trap: perpendicular axis theorem is NOT valid for 3D bodies like spheres or cylinders.
Trap: the parallel axis theorem needs one axis through the centre of mass. Check d carefully.
Shortcut: the fraction of KE that is rotational = (K²/R²) / (1 + K²/R²).
Shortcut: for a rolling solid sphere, rotational KE : translational KE = 2 : 5.
Memory: 'RDS' order of I (same M, R) is Ring > Disc > Sphere.
Memory: vertical circle, 'top 1, bottom 5', gives v² = rg at top and 5rg at bottom.
Board favourite: derive the banking angle formula, or explain the conservation of angular momentum with an example.
